Bihar Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, Bihar Economic Survey 2023-24, DGCIS (Department of Commerce), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI State Finances. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ Lakh Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~9.0%; real CAGR ~6.6%. FY24 real growth 11.5% — among the top-3 large states.

Sectoral GSVA Share — FY24[2]

Sub-sector%10-yr trend
Agriculture & Allied22↓ from 24%
Manufacturing7.5flat
Construction9↑ from 6%
Trade, Hotels, Transport27↑ from 23%
Finance, Real Estate12↑ from 9%
Public Admin & Other Svc19flat

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[4][5]

Top exports: leather & footwear (Muzaffarpur), litchi/makhana/honey, refined-petro products (Barauni), engineering goods, handicrafts.
Top imports: crude & POL, fertiliser feedstock, electronics, cement clinker, edible oils, coal. Trade deficit widened from ~$1.4B (FY15) to ~$2.6B (FY24).

2030 Objectives — Employment +10%, GDP +10%, Education 100%

Treat the three targets as linked levers: every employment intervention should also pull GDP and education indicators. Bihar's young demographic (median age ~22) means each unit of skills investment compounds for ~40 years of working life.
ObjectiveFY24 baseline2030 targetRequired CAGRPrimary levers
Employment +10% WPR 32.8% (PLFS); ~3.7 Cr workers WPR ~36%; ~4.1 Cr workers (+40 L jobs) ~1.6%/yr MSME formalisation, food-processing parks, rail/defence ancillary, tourism, IT-BPM tier-2, construction skilling
GDP +10% real (sustained) FY24 real growth 11.5%; nominal CAGR 9% Maintain ≥10% real CAGR to FY30 → GSDP ~₹15 LCr 10%/yr Manufacturing share 7.5%→14%, services depth, IWT/logistics, capex absorption (₹2.6 LCr capital outlay window)
Education ≈100% Literacy 74%, GER-HE 17%, Sec drop-out 21% Literacy ≥95%, GER-HE ≥35%, drop-out <5% ~3 pp/yr literacy Teacher hiring (2.4 L vacancies), digital classrooms, ITI/Polytechnic doubling, scholarship + transit-hostels for girls

Replicate the recipe across the 14 landmarks; the 15th (skills) is the binding constraint.

Andhra Pradesh Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, Andhra Pradesh Economic Survey 2023-24, DGCIS (Department of Commerce), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI State Finances. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ Lakh Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~8.6%; real CAGR ~5.7%. FY24 real growth 7.1% — sustained expansion driven by ports, pharma, and services.

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: petroleum & refinery products (Visakhapatnam), pharma & chemicals, seafood, rice & agri-processed goods, engineering goods, electronics/assemblies (Tirupati–Sri City–Naidupeta).
Top imports: crude oil, coal/coke, machinery & electricals, fertilizers, industrial inputs, capital goods. Trade surplus narrowed from ~$5.2B (FY15) to ~$11.1B (FY24) as imports rose faster than exports.

Strengths
  • Largest hydropower potential in India — 50 GW+ identified; Subansiri, Dibang, Kameng
  • Pristine biodiversity; 80%+ forest cover; organic-by-default agri with zero pesticide base
  • Sela Tunnel & Trans-Arunachal Highway transforming all-weather strategic connectivity
  • Act-East Policy gateway — tri-border with Bhutan, China & Myanmar; border-trade upside
Weaknesses
  • Very low industrial base; manufacturing <10% of GSVA; thin own-revenue generation
  • Hilly terrain raises logistics cost and fragments markets across 26 dispersed districts
  • Heavily dependent on Central transfers; limited private-sector investment confidence
  • Sparse population (~17/km²) constrains service viability and market scale
Strategic Potential
  • Hydro mega-projects — Subansiri Lower 2,000 MW, Dibang 2,880 MW, Kameng 600 MW online
  • Premium tourism — Tawang Buddhist circuit, Ziro valley, Mechukha, Namdapha, river rafting
  • Horticulture GI exports — kiwi, large cardamom, Apatani GI rice, oranges, mithun products
  • Stilwell Road revival and ASEAN-connectivity logistics under India's Act-East Policy

2030 Objectives — Employment +10%, GDP +10%, Education 100%

Treat the three targets as linked levers: every hydropower and tourism investment pulls jobs and GDP simultaneously; each new residential school and girls' hostel in tribal blocks compounds for decades. Arunachal's sparse geography makes human-capital investment the highest-leverage multiplier.

GDP +10% real (sustained) FY24 real growth 8.5%; nominal CAGR 11.0% Maintain ≥10% real CAGR to FY30 → GSDP ~₹0.57 LCr 10%/yr Subansiri/Dibang/Kameng hydro, transmission evacuation, roads, airport-led tourism, agri value chains, urban services around Itanagar

Assam Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, Assam Economic Survey 2023-24, DGCIS (Department of Commerce), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI State Finances. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ Lakh Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~8.0%; real CAGR ~5.1%. FY24 real growth 6.8% — steady post-COVID recovery led by oil-refinery downstream, services, and Guwahati agglomeration.

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: tea, petroleum products, petrochemicals (BCPL), agro-processed goods, border re-exports via Bangladesh/Bhutan corridors.
Top imports: crude oil feedstock, refined fuels, machinery/electricals, vehicles/spares, fertilisers, consumer goods. Trade deficit narrowed modestly from ~$0.9B (FY15) to ~$1.8B (FY24).

The three targets are linked levers: every employment intervention should also pull GDP and education indicators. Gujarat's young demographic (under-14 ~27%) and port-industrial base mean each unit of skills and logistics investment compounds for decades.

Strengths
  • India's 2nd-highest literacy (~91.6%); unified church-school network across all 11 districts

  • 30%+ bamboo-dominant forest cover — 48-year Mautam cycle drives organic-farming & biomass potential
Weaknesses
  • Jhum (shifting cultivation) degrades soil; low agri productivity and slope-erosion risk

  • Granary of India — 50%+ of national wheat & rice MSP procurement
  • Ludhiana industrial engine: hosiery, bicycles, auto-parts (Hero, Avon, Atlas, Vardhman)
  • Jalandhar GI sports goods + NRI remittance economy powering real estate & services
  • Amritsar Golden Temple — global pilgrimage capital; dairy & poultry leadership via Verka/Markfed
Weaknesses
  • Groundwater table collapsing 0.5–1 m/yr in dark-zone blocks of central Punjab
  • Paddy mono-culture, agrarian distress and mounting farm debt
  • Drug crisis and fiscal stress; emigration of youth draining productive workforce
Strategic Potential
  • Crop diversification to maize, pulses and oilseeds — break the water-guzzling paddy cycle
  • Agri-export hub via Amritsar airport, ICP Attari and DFC cold-chain linkages
  • EV + sustainable manufacturing upgrade in Ludhiana/Jalandhar MSME clusters
  • Mohali IT/biotech startup node; AYUSH and medical tourism around Patiala-Faridkot axis

Strengths

Weaknesses
  • Encircled geography — Bangladesh on 3 sides; mainland access via narrow Assam corridor

Strengths
  • Strategic location — commands Malacca Strait approaches; only tri-service Andaman & Nicobar Command
  • Port Blair harbour (Haddo-Chatham) and Veer Savarkar International Airport as UT gateway
  • Pristine beaches at Havelock/Swaraj Dweep and Neil/Shaheed Dweep; INS Kohassa airbase at Diglipur
  • Marine biodiversity: coral reefs, mangroves, Galathea Bay, leatherback turtles, Andaman Trunk Road spine
Weaknesses
  • Near-total dependence on mainland for fuel, food, cement and steel via sea freight
  • Fragile coral ecosystems; exposed to cyclones, tsunamis and sea-level rise
  • Low and thin industrial base — manufacturing only ~4% of GSVA
  • High per-unit infrastructure cost on dispersed islands; limited carrying capacity
Strategic Potential
  • Great Nicobar Mega Project: international container transshipment port, greenfield airport and power plant
  • India's Indo-Pacific pivot — blue-economy, marine biotech, ship-repair and deep-sea fishing hub
  • MICE and luxury eco-tourism with Havelock-Neil carrying-capacity model
  • Renewable microgrids, desalination and green-logistics to cut diesel import dependency

Andaman & Nicobar Islands Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, A&N Statistical Handbook 2022-23, DGCIS (Department of Commerce), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI State Finances. Values are indicative; small-UT series have wider revision bands than large-state data.

GSDP (₹ k Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~9.8%; real CAGR ~5.9%. FY24 real growth 7.3% — services-led island economy anchored by defence, tourism and fisheries.

Sectoral GSVA Share — FY24[2]

Sub-sector%10-yr trend
Agriculture & Allied15flat from 15% as fisheries and coconut offset small land base
Manufacturing4↑ from 3% through seafood, coconut and light island MSMEs
Construction13↑ from 10% on ports, jetties, roads, housing and Great Nicobar pipeline
Trade, Hotels, Transport28↑ from 22% with Port Blair airport and Havelock-Neil tourism
Finance, Real Estate9flat from 9% on small formal urban base
Public Admin & Other Svc31↓ from 38% but still defence-administration-health-education heavy

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: marine products, tuna, coconut/copra, spices, tourism receipts from Port Blair-Havelock-Neil and emerging ship/logistics services.
Top imports: fuel, food staples, cement, steel, machinery, vehicles, port/airport equipment, medicines and consumer goods. Trade deficit widened from ~$0.23B (FY15) to ~$0.67B (FY24); merchandise data is thin, while tourism and defence-logistics services are economically material.

2030 Objectives — Employment +10%, GDP +10%, Education 100%

The three targets are tightly linked in AN's small island economy: every tourism and blue-economy job directly improves per-capita GDP, while upskilling at DBRAIT, ANIIMS and ITIs serves all three levers simultaneously. The Great Nicobar pipeline — if ecological and tribal safeguards are binding — could be transformative.

Chandigarh Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, Chandigarh Statistical Abstract, DGCIS, AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI State Finances. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ k Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~9.6%; real CAGR ~6.1%. FY24 real growth 7.8% — highest per-capita income UT, compact knowledge-services economy.

Sectoral GSVA Share — FY24[2]

Sub-sector%10-yr trend
Agriculture & Allied1flat from 1% due to near-zero rural land base
Manufacturing5↓ from 7% as land-light services dominate
Construction8flat from 8% on redevelopment and tricity housing demand
Trade, Hotels, Transport25↑ from 22% with retail, airport and visitor economy
Finance, Real Estate27↑ from 24% on high-value urban property and business services
Public Admin & Other Svc34↓ from 38% but still capital, health and education heavy

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: IT/ITES and business services from IT Park, light engineering/electrical goods from Industrial Area, health-education services around PGIMER-PU-PEC and processed foods.
Top imports: electronics, vehicles, fuel, medical equipment, construction materials and consumer goods. Trade deficit widened from ~$0.47B (FY15) to ~$1.15B (FY24); services receipts are more important than merchandise trade.

Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, DH Statistical Abstract 2023-24, DGCIS, AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ k Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~12.3%; real CAGR ~7.0%. FY24 real growth 8.0% — industrial-base deepening with pharma, polymers and tourism recovery post-merger.

Manufacturing55flat-to-↑ from 53% with pharma, textiles, polymers, plastics and engineering

Trade, Hotels, Transport15↑ from 13% through Daman-Diu tourism and Mumbai-Surat logistics
Finance, Real Estate7↑ from 5% on industrial land, housing and services demand
Public Admin & Other Svc12↓ from 18% after industrial growth and UT merger scale effects

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: pharma/formulations, chemicals, textiles, polymers/plastics, packaging, engineering/electrical goods and seafood/tourism services anchored in Silvassa, Daman and Diu.
Top imports: polymer/chemical feedstock, textile inputs, machinery, electronics, fuel, packaging inputs and consumer goods. Trade surplus widened from ~$0.25B (FY15) to ~$0.80B (FY24) as the Mumbai-Surat-Vapi hinterland export base scaled.

GSDP (₹ Lakh Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~9.4%; real CAGR ~6.6%. FY24 real growth 7.4%. COVID dip in FY21 (₹7.77 L Cr) recovered strongly; FY22–FY24 compounded at ~13.1% nominal — services-led rebound anchored by IGI, NCR HQs and public spending.

Jammu & Kashmir Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, J&K Economic Survey 2023-24, DGCIS (state-of-origin exports), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ Lakh Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~8.5%; real CAGR ~5.4%. FY24 real growth 7.4% — recovering post-disruption; USBRL, Z-Morh & Zoji-La tunnels and Chenab bridge anchor the next growth cycle.

Strengths
  • 7.5 GW+ solar potential — Pang, Hanle and rooftop microgrids anchor India's first carbon-neutral UT drive
  • Strategic border location on LAC; Army/BRO logistics, Siachen approaches and defence-supply depth
  • Pashmina GI (Changthang), Kargil apricot GI and sea-buckthorn — premium niche-export products
  • World-class tourism circuit: Pangong Tso, Nubra Valley, monasteries, Hanle dark-sky reserve and world's highest motorable roads
  • Hill Development Councils (Leh & Kargil) provide district-level governance autonomy under direct Centre oversight
Weaknesses
  • 6-month snow-blockade isolates villages, raises input costs and curtails winter economic activity
  • No rail connectivity; Bilaspur–Manali–Leh railway projected beyond 2030 and terrain is extremely challenging
  • Thin-air altitude limits conventional manufacturing; plant capacity and engine efficiency fall sharply above 3,500 m
  • Heavily dependent on Central transfers — own-revenue base is thin relative to population and development spend
  • Political demand for 6th Schedule tribal-area status creates governance uncertainty for investors
Strategic Potential
  • Green hydrogen + utility solar export to mainland via HVDC — NTPC Leh pilot can anchor a multi-GW programme
  • Organic and specialty agri exports: apricot GI, Pashmina 2.0, sea-buckthorn nutraceuticals and cold-desert horticulture
  • High-altitude testing hub for defence, EV batteries, aerospace equipment and climate-resilience research
  • MICE + adventure tourism: Buddhist circuit, astronomy (Hanle), trekking and e-mobility safaris on high passes

Data compiled from MoSPI, Ladakh Statistical Handbook, DGCIS (Department of Commerce), AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States. GSDP (₹ k Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~9.7%; real CAGR ~5.8%. FY24 real growth 7.5% — construction, tourism recovery and solar investment drove the rebound post-UT bifurcation and COVID. Ladakh's small base means even modest absolute investment translates to high percentage growth.

Strengths
  • Pristine coral atolls with exceptional reef-lagoon biodiversity
  • Exclusive Economic Zone ~4 L km² — 40× the land area — rich in tuna & pelagic fish
  • Coconut & coir economy; Lakshadweep Coir GI brand recognition
  • Peaceful, homogeneous society; Schedule 5 restricted entry preserves ecology and cultural identity
Weaknesses
  • Severe land scarcity — 32 km² total, heavily built and ecologically constrained
  • Climate vulnerability: sea-level rise, coral bleaching, cyclones (Tauktae 2021)

  • Air access only via Agatti; no 24-hour emergency evacuation alternative
Strategic Potential
  • PM Mitra-tier eco-luxury tourism — India's Maldives narrative with reef-carrying-capacity discipline
  • Submarine cable & data-centre hub (proposed); strategic Arabian Sea sea-lane location
  • Tuna export cluster: pole-and-line skipjack/yellowfin cold chain, quality certification and branding
  • Blue economy: seaweed & kelp farming, Bangaram/Suheli eco-resorts, solar-plus-storage island microgrids

3Bangaram-Thinnakara-Parali lagoonLuxury resort, reef carrying-capacity and blue-carbon premium tourism★★★★★★Iconic resort lagoon can set the standard for low-volume, high-value island tourism.
4MinicoyLighthouse, Mahl culture, tuna fleet and Nine Degree Channel services★★★★★★★★Distinct culture, strategic location and fishery depth make it the southern blue-economy anchor.
5KadmatWater-sports, scuba, hospitality and reef-monitoring skill island★★★★★★★Long lagoon and existing tourism profile suit controlled adventure and conservation jobs.
6KalpeniStorm-bank, lagoon livelihood and women SHG tourism-coir compact★★★★★★Tidal/storm-bank landscape is ideal for climate education, coir and homestay upgrading.
7KiltanNorthern reef fisheries, boat services and heritage island circuit★★★★★Northern location supports fishery logistics and a less-congested heritage-tourism circuit.
8ChetlatCoir, fish landing and solar microgrid resilience pilot★★★★★Small northern island can demonstrate distributed energy and women-led livelihoods.
9BitraSmallest inhabited island, conservation-first services and emergency access★★★★Bitra's tiny scale makes carrying-capacity, telemedicine and evacuation reliability non-negotiable.
10AndrottLargest inhabited island by area, coconut-copra and heritage-services node★★★★★★Population, land area and heritage give it scope for coconut value addition and public-service depth.
11AminiCoir craft, boat-building traditions and skills-to-market channel★★★★★★Amini's craft base can connect Lakshadweep Coir GI with e-commerce and tourism retail.
12Kavaratti-Agatti-Minicoy solar beltSolar-plus-storage, desalination and diesel-displacement mission★★★★★★★★High diesel cost and strong sun make clean island energy one of the highest-return interventions.
13Tuna landing & canning cooperativesSkipjack/yellowfin cold chain, quality certification and export branding★★★★★★★★Tuna is the UT's most scalable productive livelihood if value addition happens before mainland shipping.
14Kochi-Beypore-Mangaluru shipping interfacePassenger-cargo reliability, cold chain and medical evacuation logistics★★★★★Mainland connectivity determines prices, emergency care, tourism reliability and export quality.
15Lakshadweep Coir GI clusterWomen-led coir, coconut fibre design and premium island craft retail★★★★★★★GI branding can lift incomes from a traditional sector without stressing reefs or land.
Sequencing recipe: (1) tourism/fisheries/solar anchor tenant + (2) marine-skills and ITI/polytechnic satellite co-location + (3) plug into Agatti airport plus Kochi-Beypore-Mangaluru shipping + (4) tuna-coir-copra-GI export channel + (5) girls' hostels, tele-education and island-safe transport.

Puducherry Growth Atlas — 4 Districts, 4 Non-Contiguous Enclaves

A one-page-per-district lens on Puducherry's growth potential — strengths, weaknesses, geographical & skill advantages, industry presence, employment ecosystem, plus green-energy and water-recharge opportunities. Puducherry is a Union Territory with legislature: elected Legislative Assembly + Lieutenant Governor; its four non-contiguous enclaves (Puducherry in TN, Karaikal in TN, Mahe in KL, Yanam in AP) span three neighbouring states. Strengths
  • High HDI and among the highest per-capita NSDP in peninsular India (~₹2.4 L)
  • French-heritage tourism — White Town, Promenade, Auroville-Matrimandir global brand
  • JIPMER + Pondicherry University: national medical and higher-education anchors
  • Manufacturing clusters (PIPDIC/SIPCOT estates): auto components, electronics, leather, textiles, chemicals, pharma
Weaknesses
  • Four non-contiguous enclaves (Mahe in KL, Yanam in AP, Karaikal in TN) — administrative and planning fragmentation
  • Dependent on Tamil Nadu for water (Krishna water-sharing) and road/rail hinterland access
  • Revenue skewed to liquor/tourism receipts; narrow economic base limits resilience
  • Limited land area (492 km²) across four separate territories constrains large-scale industrialisation
Strategic Potential
  • Auroville–Sri Aurobindo wellness-spiritual circuit: premium global tourism and design-craft exports
  • Karaikal Port expansion — minor-port gateway for delta seafood, agri-produce and bulk cargo
  • Fintech + IT/ITES scale-up (Indira Nagar tech park) leveraging Chennai proximity and Pondicherry University talent
  • Aerospace components cluster as an extension of Chennai–Coimbatore belt via PIPDIC estates

Puducherry Economy — A 10-Year Lens (FY15 → FY24)

Data compiled from MoSPI, Puducherry Statistical Handbook 2023-24, DGCIS, AISHE, UDISE+, and RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States. Values are indicative; minor revisions occur in successive vintages.

GSDP (₹ k Crore, current prices)[1]

10-yr nominal CAGR ~10.1%; real CAGR ~6.3%. FY24 real growth 7.2% — services and tourism recovery post-COVID; FY21 dip reflects enclave-economy vulnerability. Units: ₹ thousand crore (k Cr).

Sectoral GSVA Share — FY24[2]

Sub-sector%10-yr trend
Agriculture & Allied5↓ from 7% as services and urbanisation outpace farm output
Manufacturing22flat from 22% with leather, textiles, chemicals, food and pharma MSMEs
Construction13↑ from 10% on tourism, housing, port and public works
Trade, Hotels, Transport28↑ from 24% via tourism, liquor retail, port and cross-border commerce
Finance, Real Estate12↑ from 10% on urban services and education/health demand
Public Admin & Other Svc20↓ from 27% but still high due to UT administration, health and education

Exports & Imports (US$ Million)[3]

Top exports: leather/footwear, textiles, chemicals/pharma, marine products, rice/food products and high-value tourism, education and medical services anchored in Puducherry and Karaikal.
Top imports: petroleum products, machinery, chemicals, electronics, textile inputs, edible oils and construction/port cargo. Trade deficit widened from ~$0.22B (FY15) to ~$0.36B (FY24); UT-level merchandise data is small and services receipts are material.

Puducherry's strongest gain is high GER, near-universal school infrastructure and medical/university depth around JIPMER and Pondicherry University. The persistent gap is Yanam's lower literacy/skills base and the need to convert high education access into local formal jobs.

2030 Objectives — Employment +10%, GDP +10%, Education 100%

Treat the three targets as linked levers: every employment intervention should also pull GDP and education indicators. Puducherry's enclave structure means each anchor investment in one district must be paired with skills pipelines that reach the other three.
